HTML Video

❮ Previous Try Adventure Mode Next ❯
Share

HTML <video> Element

The HTML <video> element is used to show a video on a web page.

It supports playback controls like play, pause, volume, and fullscreen.

Example

The HTML code:

<video width="400" controls>
  <source src="mov_bbb.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="mov_bbb.ogg" type="video/ogg">
  Your browser does not support HTML video.
</video>

Result

Video courtesy of Big Buck Bunny.

Try it Yourself »

HTML <video> Attributes

The controls attribute adds video controls, like play, pause, volume and full screen.

It is also a good idea to include width and height attributes. If height and width are not set, the page might flicker while the video loads.

The <source> element allows you to specify alternative video files the browser may choose from. The browser will use the first recognized format.

The text between the <video> and </video> tags will only be displayed in browsers that do not support the <video> element.

HTML <video> Autoplay

To start a video automatically, use the autoplay attribute:

Example

<video controls width="320" height="240" autoplay>
  <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="movie.ogg" type="video/ogg">
Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
Try it Yourself »

Tip: Add muted after autoplay to let your video start playing automatically (but muted):

Example

<video controls width="320" height="240" autoplay muted>
  <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="movie.ogg" type="video/ogg">
Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
Try it Yourself »

HTML <video> Loop

The loop attribute specifies that the video will start over again, every time it is finished:

Example

<video controls width="320" height="240" autoplay loop>
  <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="movie.ogg" type="video/ogg">
Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
Try it Yourself »

Supported Video Formats in HTML5

The supported video formats in HTML are:

Video Format File Extension Media Type
MPEG-4
or MP4		 .mp4 video/mp4
Ogg .ogg video/ogg
WebM .webm video/webm

HTML <video> and JavaScript

The HTML DOM defines methods, properties, and events for the <video> element.

This allows you to load, play, and pause videos, as well as setting duration and volume.

There are also DOM events that can notify you when a video begins to play, is paused, etc.

Example: Using JavaScript

Try it Yourself »

For a full DOM reference, go to our HTML Audio/Video DOM Reference.

HTML Video Tags

Tag Description
<video> Defines a video or movie
<source> Defines multiple media resources for media elements, such as <video> and <audio>
<track> Defines text tracks in media players
